steps.body: You already know the rounding rule: check the neighbor digit one spot to the right of where you're rounding. **That rule never changes, no matter how far left you round.** Rounding 428,619 to the nearest thousand? Check the hundreds digit (6). Since 6 ≥ 5, round up: **429,000.**
Rounding is a question about which side you are on.

widget.prompt: Place 46,800 on the line. Then look at which end of the line it is nearer.
widget.successFeedback: 46,800 sits past the halfway mark of 45,000, so it is nearer 50,000 than 40,000 — that is what 'rounds up to 50,000' MEANS. Rounding is not a rule about the digit 6; it is a question about which side of halfway you landed.
widget.lowFeedback: Your marker is below 46,800. Slide it right.
widget.highFeedback: Your marker is above 46,800. Slide it left.

predict.prompt: Before you place it: is 46800 closer to 40000 or to 50000?
predict.reveal: 46800 sits 6800 from 40000 and 3200 from 50000 — the 50000 side wins. Judging position from the endpoints first makes the exact placement easier to defend.

explanationVariants: The hundreds digit in 428,619 is 6, which is ≥5, so the thousands digit rounds up: 429,000.
Checking one place right of the thousands (the hundreds digit, 6) triggers a round-up to 429,000.

commonErrors.feedback: 428,000 rounds down — but the hundreds digit (6) is 5 or more, which rounds UP: 429,000.
428,600 only rounds to the nearest hundred, not the nearest thousand. Rounding to the thousand gives 429,000.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Check the hundreds digit (one place right of thousands) to decide up or down.

steps.body: The same rule climbs even higher: round to the nearest **ten-thousand** by checking the **thousands** digit. For 428,619: the thousands digit is 8, which is ≥5, so round up: **430,000.**

explanationVariants: The thousands digit in 652,340 is 2, which is <5, so the ten-thousands digit stays the same: 650,000.
Checking the thousands digit (2) triggers a round-down to 650,000.

commonErrors.feedback: 660,000 rounds up — but the thousands digit (2) is less than 5, which rounds DOWN: 650,000.
652,000 only rounds to the nearest thousand, not ten-thousand. Rounding to the ten-thousand gives 650,000.

explanationVariants: The hundreds digit in 345,500 is exactly 5 — by the honest halfway convention, that rounds up: 346,000.
Exactly halfway always follows the agreed rule: round up.

commonErrors.feedback: 345,000 rounds down — but exactly halfway (hundreds digit 5) follows the convention of rounding UP: 346,000.
350,000 rounds to the nearest ten-thousand, not thousand. Rounding to the thousand gives 346,000.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A hundreds digit of exactly 5 rounds up, by the same convention you already know.

hints: Check the hundreds digit: it's 6, which is 5 or more.
Rounding up the thousands digit means 999 thousands become 1,000 thousands.
explanationVariants: The hundreds digit (6) rounds up; 999 thousand rounds up to 1,000 thousand — which is exactly 1,000,000. The round-up carries all the way through.
Rounding 999,600 to the nearest thousand rolls every digit over into a brand-new million.

commonErrors.feedback: 999,000 rounds down — but the hundreds digit (6) is ≥5, which rounds UP. Rounding up 999 thousand carries all the way to 1,000,000.
That keeps digits that rounding is meant to clear. Rounding to the nearest thousand zeros out everything after: 1,000,000.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Round up the thousands digit from 999 — watch what happens when it carries.

takeaways: Always check the digit exactly one place to the right of your rounding target.
5 or more rounds up; less than 5 rounds down; exactly 5 follows the honest convention of rounding up.
A round-up can carry through every digit — even rolling all the way into a new million.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Check the digit one place to the right of your target, no matter which place you're rounding to.** For 4,700 rounded to the nearest thousand: check the hundreds digit (7). Since 7 ≥ 5, round up: 5,000.

explanationVariants: The hundreds digit (7) is ≥5, so 4,700 rounds up to 5,000.
Checking the hundreds digit triggers a round-up.

options.feedback: The hundreds digit (7) is ≥5 — rounds up to 5,000.
4,000 rounds down — but the hundreds digit (7) is 5 or more, which rounds up: 5,000.
That's the original number, not rounded at all. To the nearest thousand, it's 5,000.
